title: Unique Email Addresses
summary: Each valid email includes a local name and a domain name, separated by '@'.
statement: Each valid email includes a local name and a domain name, separated by '@'. The local name can have periods '.' or a plus '+' which affect forwarding rules. Periods are ignored in the local name, but plus signs ignore everything after the first one. These rules do not affect the domain name. Given an array of email addresses, count the unique addresses that receive emails.
constraints: In the local part, dots are ignored and text after the first plus is ignored.
The domain is unchanged; count distinct delivered addresses.
hints: Normalize only the local portion; domain rules are different.
Split at @, truncate local at +, remove local dots, then reattach domain.
Insert each normalized address into a set.
Exactly addresses with the same normalized local and identical domain share delivery.
editorial: Exactly addresses with the same normalized local and identical domain share delivery.

tests.explanation: The first two normalize together; the third has a different domain, giving two.
The three distinct local parts remain distinct.
